headline: Enriquez Takes Asian Games Jiu-Jitsu Silver, PH Total Hits 29
seoTitle: Enriquez Wins Asian Games Jiu-Jitsu Silver; PH Reaches 29 | FMB News
seoDescription: Alexandria Enriquez won the women's 63kg jiu-jitsu silver as the Philippines reached 29 medals at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games.
deck: The women's 63kg final was decided by a single advantage after a scoreless regulation result; the medal is final, not merely assured.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: Alexandria Nicole Enriquez won silver in the women's 63kg jiu-jitsu event at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games on Saturday, October 3, after a narrow final against Thailand's Orapa Senatham.

GMA News and The Philippine Star reported that the match ended 0-0 on points and was decided by Senatham's single advantage. Enriquez had submitted all three of her earlier opponents before the final.

sections.heading: Final medal, not an assurance
paragraphs: This is a completed silver-medal result. It is distinct from merely reaching a medal round or being assured at least bronze.
Andrea Lao did not add a medal in the women's 52kg division after losing the bronze-medal match 0-2 to Mongolia's Narankhishig Baasanjargal.

sections.heading: Philippine tally
paragraphs: Independent Philippine reports placed the delegation at four golds, nine silvers and 16 bronzes after Enriquez's result, or 29 medals in total. The count was current on October 3 and was not described as the final delegation total while events remained.

Enriquez delivered the jiu-jitsu team's second medal after Kaila Napolis won bronze. Earlier FMB News coverage recorded the Philippines at 28 medals after Jeus Yape's virtual taekwondo gold: /news/jeus-yape-asian-games-gold-medal-rush-october-2-2026/.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: The result gave the Philippines a ninth silver and extended a multi-sport medal surge at the Games. The clean distinction between an assured medal and a final result matters because medal-table totals should change only after the relevant contest is completed.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Watch the official Games results and medal table for the closing Philippine total, plus any remaining Filipino events. Later results may change the 4-9-16 count.

verificationNotes: The official Aichi-Nagoya results portal was used as the competition reference.
GMA News independently confirms Enriquez's final silver and the Philippine 4-9-16 tally.
The Philippine Star independently confirms the scoreless points result, Senatham's deciding advantage and Lao's 0-2 bronze-match loss.
The article explicitly labels Enriquez's medal as final and does not count Lao as a medalist.
The medal table is time-bounded to October 3 and not described as the final delegation total.
Available event photography lacked independently verified reuse permission, so FMB's owned fallback is used and labeled non-documentary.
